facts.statement: The genus Shantungosuchus was first described by Yang in 1961.
Shantungosuchus is an extinct crocodyliform genus found in China during the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Shantungosuchus is an extinct genus of Early Cretaceous crocodyliform found in China.

facts.statement: The genus includes three species: S. chuhsienensis and S. brachycephalus described by Yang Zhongjian in 1961 and 1982, and S. hangjinensis described by Xiao-Chun Wu et al. in 1994.
facts.quote: It includes three species: Shantungosuchus chuhsienensis and S. brachycephalus, which were both described by Yang Zhongjian – usually referred to as "Young" – in 1961 and 1982, and S. hangjinensis, which was described by Xiao-Chun Wu et al in 1994.

facts.statement: The name Shantungosuchus derives from Shandong, the Chinese province where the animal was first discovered.
facts.quote: The primary part of Shantungosuchus name comes from Shan-tung, the Wade-Giles romanization of Shandong (), a province located on the eastern coast of the People's Republic of China, where it was first discovered.

facts.statement: The suffix 'suchus' in the name refers to the Ancient Greek word for the Egyptian crocodile deity Sobek.
facts.quote: The second part, suchus is an Ancient Greek word referring to the Egyptian crocodile deity Sobek that is commonly used as a suffix for crocodylomorph genera and crocodile-like animals in general.

facts.statement: The type species, S. chuhsienensis, was originally described from an articulated skeleton preserved as a ventral impression.
facts.quote: Shantungosuchus chuhsienenis was first described from an articulated skeleton that was preserved as an impression of its ventral surface.

facts.statement: The total length of S. chuhsienensis is approximately 30 cm.
facts.quote: Its total length is only about 30 cm.

facts.statement: The group Protosuchia is now considered a paraphyletic grouping of early crocodyliforms.
facts.quote: Protosuchia has recently been considered a paraphyletic grouping of early crocodyliforms.

facts.statement: Protosuchia is commonly divided into the basal family Protosuchidae and a group of basal crocodyliforms related to Hsisosuchus and Mesoeucrocodylia.
facts.quote: Protosuchia is now commonly split into two groups: the basal family Protosuchidae, which is a true clade, and a group of basal crocodyliforms more closely related to Hsisosuchus and Mesoeucrocodylia.

facts.statement: Research by Clark et al. (2004) and Buscalioni (2017) places Shantungosuchus in the superfamily Shartegosuchoidea, grouping it with Sichuanosuchus and Shartegosuchidae.
facts.quote: Clark et al. (2004) recovered Shantungosuchus as closely related to mesoeucrocodylians, and Buscalioni (2017) found the genus to group in a clade with Sichuanosuchus and Shartegosuchidae, which was formally named Shartegosuchoidea by Dollman et al. (2018) in their description of a new Shartegosuchus specimen.

facts.statement: S. chuhsienensis lived during the Early Cretaceous (Barremian-Aptian) in the Mengyin Formation of Shandong province.
facts.quote: Shantungosuchus chuhsienensis has been found in the Early Cretaceous (Barremian-Aptian) Mengyin Formation of Shandong province.

facts.statement: S. hangjinensis lived in the lower Cretaceous Luohandong Formation of Outer Mongolia, while S. brachycephalus may also have lived in that region.
facts.quote: S. hangjinensis, however, is slightly younger, and is found in the lower Cretaceous Luohandong Formation of Outer Mongolia, and S. brachycephalus may also have been found in the same region.

facts.statement: Fossils found in the Luohandong Formation suggest S. hangjinensis shared its habitat with fish like Sinamia, the turtle Ordosemys, the crocodyliform Ikechosaurus, and various unidentified dinosaurs.
facts.quote: The Luohandong formation provides clues to the environment of Shantungosuchus. For instance, S. hangjinensis likely shared its habitat with fish such as Sinamia, the turtle Ordosemys, and another species of crocodile-like reptile called Ikechosaurus, and several types of dinosaurs- though none have been identified to the level of genus.

facts.statement: The genus Shantungosuchus lived between 143.1 and 125.77 million years ago, from the Berriasian to the Hauterivian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Berriasian to Hauterivian (143.1 to 125.77 million years ago)

facts.statement: Shantungosuchus belongs to the parent group Shartegosuchoidea.
Shantungosuchus is classified within the class Reptilia.

There is an ongoing debate regarding the classification of Shantungosuchus, with some authors suggesting it is an atoposaurid while others, like Xiao-Chun Wu, argue it belongs to the family Protosuchidae.
facts.quote: Since the description of S. chuhsienensis, there has been uncertainty about the placement of the genus. It was suggested to be an atoposaurid by several different authors from the 1960s to the 1980s,. However, in Xiao-Chun Wu's 1994 description of S. hangjinensis, he noted the bones were more similar to the family Protosuchidae rather than Atoposauridae, and proposed to classify it as such.

rejected.statement: S. chuhsienensis is characterized by its small size, slender body, and triangular skull.
rejected.quote: Its small size, slender body, and triangular skull made it distinct from other atoposaurids.
